text:
ROXANE (seeing that the door is being opened):
  Let us go in! . . .
  (From the threshold, to Cyrano):
  If Christian comes, as I presume he will,
  Tell him to wait for me!

CYRANO (quickly, as she is about to disappear):
  Ah! . . .
  (She turns around):
  On what, as is your custom,
  Do you intend to question him today?

ROXANE:
  On. . .

CYRANO (quickly):
  On?

ROXANE:
  But you will keep silent about it!

CYRANO:
  Like a wall.

ROXANE:
  On nothing! . . .I shall tell him: Go on! Give yourself free rein!
  Improvise. Speak of love. Be splendid!

CYRANO (smiling):
  Good.

ROXANE:
  Hush! . . .

CYRANO:
  Hush! . . .

ROXANE:
  Not a word! . . .
  (She goes inside and closes the door again.)

CYRANO (bowing to her once the door is closed):
  With my thanks.
  (The door opens again and Roxane puts her head out.)

ROXANE:
  He might prepare himself! . . .

CYRANO:
  Good heavens, no! . . .

BOTH (together):
  Hush! . . .
  (The door closes.)

CYRANO (calling):
  Christian!



Scene 3.IV.

Cyrano, Christian.


CYRANO:
  I know everything that is needed. Prepare thy memory.
  Here is the opportunity to cover ourselves with glory.
  Let us waste no time. Do not look so sullen.
  Quickly, let us go back to thy place; I am going to teach thee. . .

CHRISTIAN:
  No!

CYRANO:
  What?

CHRISTIAN:
  No! I am waiting for Roxane here.

CYRANO:
  What madness
  Has seized thee? Come quickly and learn. . .

CHRISTIAN:
  No, I tell thee!
  I am weary of borrowing my letters and my speeches,
  And of playing this part, and of always trembling! . . .
  It was fine at first! But I feel that she loves me!
  Thank thee. I am no longer afraid. I shall speak for myself.

CYRANO:
  Indeed!

CHRISTIAN:
  And who tells thee that I would not know how? . . .
  I am not so stupid, after all! Thou shalt see!
  But, my dear fellow, thy lessons have been useful to me.
  I shall know how to speak alone! And, by all the devils,
  I shall certainly always know how to take her in my arms! . . .
  (Catching sight of Roxane, who is coming out of Clomire's house):
  —There she is! Cyrano, no, do not leave me!

CYRANO (bowing to him):
  Speak by yourself, sir.
  (He disappears behind the garden wall.)



Scene 3.V.

Christian, Roxane, several male and female précieuses, and the duenna,
for a moment.


ROXANE (leaving Clomire's house with a company from whom she is taking
  her leave: curtsies and bows):
  Barthenoïde!—Alcandre!—Grémione! . . .

THE DUENNA (in despair):
  We missed the discourse on Tenderness!
  (She goes into Roxane's house.)

ROXANE (still taking leave):
  Urimédonte! . . .Farewell! . . .
  (They all bow to Roxane, bow again to one another, part, and
  go off along different streets. Roxane sees Christian):
  It is you! . . .
  (She goes to him):
  Evening is falling.
  Wait. They are far away. The air is mild. No passersby.
  Let us sit down. Speak. I am listening.

CHRISTIAN (sits down near her on the bench. A silence):
  I love you.

ROXANE (closing her eyes):
  Yes, speak to me of love.

CHRISTIAN:
  I love thee.

ROXANE:
  That is the theme.
  Embroider, embroider.

CHRISTIAN:
  I. . .you. . .

ROXANE:
  Embroider!

CHRISTIAN:
  I love thee so much.

ROXANE:
  No doubt! And then?

CHRISTIAN:
  And then. . .I would be so happy
  If you loved me!—Tell me, Roxane, that thou lovest me!

ROXANE (pouting):
  You offer me gruel when I had hoped for creams!
  Tell me how you love me. . .

CHRISTIAN:
  Why. . .very much.

ROXANE:
  Oh! . . .Unlabyrinth your feelings!

CHRISTIAN (having moved closer and devouring the fair nape of her neck with his eyes):
  Thy neck!
  I would like to kiss it! . . .

ROXANE:
  Christian!

CHRISTIAN:
  I love thee!

ROXANE (trying to rise):
  Again!

CHRISTIAN (quickly, holding her back):
  No! I do not love thee!

ROXANE (sitting down again):
  That is fortunate!

CHRISTIAN:
  I adore thee!

ROXANE (rising and moving away):
  Oh!

CHRISTIAN:
  Yes. . .I am becoming a fool!

ROXANE (dryly):
  And that displeases me!
  As it would displease me if you were to become ugly.

CHRISTIAN:
  But. . .

ROXANE:
  Go and gather up your fleeing eloquence!

CHRISTIAN:
  I. . .

ROXANE:
  You love me, I know. Farewell.
  (She goes toward the house.)

CHRISTIAN:
  Not yet!
  I shall tell you. . .

ROXANE (pushing the door open to go inside):
  That you adore me. . .yes, I know.
  No! No! Go away!

CHRISTIAN:
  But I. . .
  (She shuts the door in his face.)

CYRANO (who came back in some time ago without being seen):
  It is a success.



Scene 3.VI.

Christian, Cyrano, the pages, for a moment.


CHRISTIAN:
  Help!

CYRANO:
  No, sir.

CHRISTIAN:
  I shall die if I do not regain
  Her favor this very instant. . .

CYRANO:
  And how the devil can I
  Make you learn this very instant? . . .

CHRISTIAN (seizing his arm):
  Oh! There, look, see!
  (The balcony window has lit up.)

CYRANO (moved):
  Her window!

CHRISTIAN (shouting):
  I am going to die!

CYRANO:
  Lower your voice!

CHRISTIAN (very softly):
  Die! . . .

CYRANO:
  The night is dark. . .

CHRISTIAN:
  Well?

CYRANO:
  It can be repaired.
  You do not deserve it. . .Stand there, wretch!
  There, in front of the balcony! I shall stand underneath. . .
  And prompt thee with thy words.

CHRISTIAN:
  But. . .

CYRANO:
  Be silent!

THE PAGES (reappearing at the back, to Cyrano):
  Hey!

CYRANO:
  Hush! . . .
  (He motions to them to speak quietly.)

FIRST PAGE (in a low voice):
  We have just serenaded
  Montfleury! . . .

CYRANO (quietly, quickly):
  Go and lie in ambush,
  One at that street corner and the other at this one;
  And if some troublesome passerby comes this way,
  Play a tune!

SECOND PAGE:
  What tune, Mr. Gassendist?

CYRANO:
  A merry one for a woman, and for a man, a sad one!
  (The pages disappear, one at each street corner.—To Christian):
  Call her!

CHRISTIAN:
  Roxane!

CYRANO (picking up pebbles, which he throws at the windowpanes):
  Wait! A few pebbles.



Scene VII.

Roxane, Christian, Cyrano, at first hidden beneath the balcony.


ROXANE (partly opening her window):
  Who is calling me?

CHRISTIAN:
  I am.

ROXANE:
  Who is “I”?

CHRISTIAN:
  Christian.

ROXANE (with disdain):
  It is you?
